entry.title: EMACS Text Editor Turns 50
entry.content:
Links: technologyreview.com | hacker news

Originally created at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory in 1976, the EMACS text editor is celebrating its 50th anniversary and remains widely used today. Developed initially as a set of macros for the TECO editor by researchers including Richard Stallman, Guy Steele Jr., and David Moon, EMACS provided a standardized, customizable full-screen editing experience that transformed how programmers interacted with computers.

The software-sharing culture surrounding early versions of EMACS directly influenced the emergence of the free software movement and the creation of the GNU Project. Over the decades, variants of the software were commercialized by companies like Honeywell and James Gosling, while others were integrated into operating systems such as Unix and early versions of Mac OS X, leaving a lasting legacy on modern software development environments.

Durman's case follows a similar exemption secured by a Unitarian Universalist software engineer and arrives amid growing legal and ethical discussions regarding workplace AI mandates and broader societal skepticism toward automated technologies.

entry.title: Apple Developer Tools on macOS Still Trust Compromised eMudhra Certificates
entry.content:
Links: emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com | hacker news

Developer tools bundled with macOS—including git, curl, and python3—continue to trust compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates more than a week after Apple was notified of the security incident. Additionally, the recent release of macOS 27.2 failed to address the issue and overwrote manual workarounds applied by users, leaving development environments vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks.

This trust flaw allows attackers to intercept HTTPS connections, tamper with repository clones and pushes, and capture sensitive credentials like GitHub tokens. While Apple has secured Safari and applications using its core networking framework, developers must manually remove the affected root certificates and reapply fixes after system updates until an official patch is issued.

entry.title: Ellia Lebleu Discusses Wikipedia's Ongoing Cleanup of AI-Generated Content
entry.content:
Links: spectrum.ieee.org | hacker news

In an interview with IEEE Spectrum, WikiProject AI Cleanup founding member Ellia Lebleu discusses the volunteer efforts launched in late 2023 to detect and remove artificial intelligence-generated material from Wikipedia. Lebleu notes that while early AI content was marked by glaring clichés and predictable structures, modern machine-generated submissions have become increasingly subtle, often featuring faulty citations and nuanced rhetorical patterns.

Despite the English Wikipedia's policy prohibiting large language models for content generation, volunteers estimate that AI text still accounts for a notable percentage of new drafts and submissions. The project relies on developing detection tools, automated verifiers, and coordination with the Wikimedia Foundation, raising broader questions about maintaining Wikipedia as a uniquely human-written corpus in an era dominated by generative AI.
